title: Seven odds leave one
hook: Pick any seven odd numbers you like. Can you make them add up to an even total?

knows: which whole numbers are odd and which are even
doesNotKnow: why the rules for adding odd and even numbers hold

misconception: Odd and even rules are facts to memorise, or the parity of a sum depends on which numbers you pick.
objective: The learner can explain, using leftover dots, that a sum of odd numbers is odd exactly when there is an odd count of them, whatever the numbers are.

claims.text: Every odd number is some pairs plus one leftover: 2k + 1.
claims.source: Definition of an odd whole number.

claims.text: The sum of seven odd numbers is always odd: the seven leftovers make three pairs and one alone.
claims.source: Sum of (2k_i + 1) over seven terms = 2(sum of k_i) + 7 = 2(sum of k_i + 3) + 1.

claims.text: A sum of odd numbers has the parity of how many there are, so an even count of odd numbers gives an even total.
claims.source: Sum of n terms (2k_i + 1) = 2(sum of k_i) + n, which has the parity of n.
Recomputed with node; the stage computes its total with the same sum() it displays.

recall.question: You add up 10 odd numbers. Without knowing them, what can you say about the total?
recall.why: Each odd number has one leftover dot after pairing. Ten leftovers pair off completely, so the total is even.
